summary: This bill requires the Director of the Office of Management and Budget to review whether the "lowest price technically acceptable" source selection process in federal acquisition regulations creates national security risks for Defense and Civilian agencies and to report the findings to Congress.

scores.thoughts: The bill requires OMB to review federal procurement practices (specifically the lowest price technically acceptable source selection process) across Defense and Civilian agencies for national security risks and issue a report. While this touches on how the government spends money through procurement, the bill itself mandates no changes to spending levels, appropriations, or budget authority—it is limited to a one-time review and reporting requirement. Therefore, it has no meaningful bearing on expanding or reducing government spending.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, tax policy, or revenue collection. It is exclusively focused on a procurement review.
